newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana birthday tremor may presage worse - expert.
newsitem.headline: Ghana birthday tremor may presage worse - expert.

text.p: An earth tremor shook parts of Ghana's capital Accra on Thursday, the West African nation's 40th birthday, rattling buildings and sending people running into the street.
There were no immediate reports of serious injury or damage but an independent geologist predicted that the tremor, the third this year, could presage worse to come.
Charles Oduro, director of the Geological Survey Department, told Reuters the tremor measured 4.5 on the open-ended Richter scale and was the third of that magnitude in three months.
Jan van Landewijk, an independent geologist and researcher in the West African country since 1958, said worse could be on the way.

"I am afraid that these are pre-shocks to a major shocks. All indicators are in the red. The intensity of the shocks is getting bigger each time," he told Reuters. "We must prepare for an earthquake of about 6.5 on the scale of Richter."
Accra is on a junction of two major and two minor fault lines. The tremors were the strongest since 1969.
In 1939, an earthquake estimated by some of 6.5, by others of 8.0 on Richter scale, killed 16 people and injured 133 in Accra. Buildings were damaged or partially collapsed.
Van Landewijk, a Dutch national, works as a geology lecturer and researcher at the University of Ghana.
"In fact a major shock is overdue, as we are registering pre-shocks of increasing magnitude since 1964," he said.
On February 14, a tremor measured at between 4.1 and 5.0 on Richter scale shook Accra and its environs. On January 8, there was a tremor of between 3.8 and 4.5.
Ghana gained independence from Britain on March 6, 1957, becoming the first British dependency in Sub-Saharan Africa to attain independence under majority rule.
A seismological report from the Geological Survey Department last year said a major quake should not be ruled out.
"The occurance of the 1939 earthquake and recent micro-seismic activities indicate that the occurance of another major earthquake should not be ruled out," it said.
